metadata.title: AI's Speed Crash: The Structural Bull Market Isn't Over
metadata.speaker: Jordi Visser

executive_takeaway: (1) The AI structural bull market is intact but we are in a 'speed crash' / midcycle digestion phase: the Morgan Stanley tech momentum factor fell ~40% in 18 days, the worst tech unwind on record back to 1998. (2) Visser frames the new market regime as 'bubbles, parabolas, and speed crashes' driven by AI agents now executing non-emotional, momentum-chasing trades with leverage ('V control') that unwind violently. (3) He is buying selectively into weakness - added Micron this week, calls 'AI = memory' - but says odds are now 'fair' so he is sitting out the race until better setups. (4) He expects no massive V-shaped bounce; the correction is a healthy rotation, not a 2007-style systemic event - junk spreads are tight, earnings beats are huge, economy is strong. (5) His forward beta for the next 12 months is crypto/consumer agents (Ethereum especially), not the infrastructure trade; he sees Bitcoin as 'collateral of the future' and AGI arriving within a few years.

risks: Auto-generated transcript (yt-dlp); some names garbled (e.g. 'Kimi K 3.0', 'Integris', 'Fluence', 'Kimors', 'Marll'=Marvell, 'V control'=VaR control, 'VA'=variance). Verify tickers independently.
Visser is a market participant with positions; his bullish structural view may be self-reinforced by his book (owns MU, NVDA, MRVL, LLY).
He dismisses the 'AI debt situation' as non-risk; others (Zero Hedge cited) flag hyperscaler leverage as systemic - contested.
His 'no recession' call rests on S&P YoY not going negative; a sharp drawdown could flip that signal quickly.
Comparing current tech unwind to 2007 ignores that spreads are tight and earnings are beating - but 'as good as it gets' historically precedes tops.
AGI-by-2030 and 'public companies won't survive' are speculative convictions, not analysis; treat as opinion.
Crypto call (next-12mo beta) depends on breaking the 200-day MA, which he admits may not happen before Oct/Nov and could make new lows first.
His 'optimized portfolio bubble' / AI-agent market-structure thesis is novel and untested across a full cycle.
Software names called 'toast' (Adobe, Salesforce) may pivot successfully; his 200-day-MA read is technical, not fundamental.
Past analogs (Amazon 2013, Nvidia 2023 head-and-shoulders) may not repeat for Micron.

actionable_takeaways.item: Treat the AI selloff as a 'speed crash' / digestion, not the end of the structural bull - but don't expect a V-shaped bounce
'AI = memory': monitor DRAM prices and memory shortage as the binding constraint on the buildout
Use VWAP + first-hour volume on 60-min charts to spot real bottoms (Micron reclaimed VWAP on biggest volume since peak)
Watch for head-and-shoulders neckline break then immediate reclaim as highest-conviction buy in structural bulls
Next 12-month beta is crypto/consumer agents (Ethereum especially), not re-entering infrastructure
Read Demis Hassabis' AGI essay; he is the most honest voice on the timeline (~2030)
Ignore backward-looking inflation data; Warsh is reformist not hawkish - likely rate cuts ahead
Verify ticker names (Marvell, Integris, Fluence, etc.) and garbled transcript segments independently
Watch junk spreads and S&P YoY as recession signals - both still healthy
